reason: The quote states you can use multiple target tracking scaling policies together, provided that each of them uses a different metric.
The quote states target tracking removes the need to manually define CloudWatch alarms and scaling adjustments, handled automatically from the target you set.
Under Considerations the quote states you can't use a target tracking policy to scale out when the specified metric is below the target value.
The quote states scale out if any target tracking policy is ready to scale out, and scale in only if all policies with scale in enabled are ready.
The quotes give predefined or custom metrics and the four list items; the context shows the predefined list holds exactly these four and that custom metrics are other CloudWatch metrics.
The quote states target tracking prioritizes availability by scaling in more gradually when traffic is decreasing, and points to step scaling for greater control.
The quote states that to scale in to 0 when no requests are routed, the group's minimum capacity must be set to 0.
The quote states EC2 Auto Scaling creates and manages the CloudWatch alarms that invoke scaling events when the metric deviates from the target.
The quote states to use resources cost efficiently, set the target value as high as possible with a reasonable buffer for unexpected traffic increases.
The quote states that for throughput metrics such as ALB request count per target, the target value is the optimal average throughput from a single instance for a one-minute period.

The quotes say RequestCount and Latency do not work for target tracking, but for Latency they say it 'doesn't necessarily change proportionally' and can increase with utilization; the claim drops the hedge and says both 'do not change in proportion'.
The quote gives the Terminating, Terminating:Wait, Terminating:Proceed (after completing the lifecycle action) and Terminated sequence for an EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING hook.
Under Scale in the quote states the group uses its termination policy to choose instances, and terminating instances enter Terminating and can't be put back into service.
The quote states EC2 Auto Scaling always balances across Availability Zones first regardless of termination policy, so some newer instances might be terminated before older ones.
The quote and context state that after the outdated-configuration criteria the default policy picks the instance closest to the next billing hour, and one at random when equally close.
The quote states the default termination policy is designed to terminate instances using outdated configurations first, and that you can change the termination policy.
Under the default policy heading the quote states it first identifies the Availability Zone with the most instances and at least one instance not protected from scale in.
The quote states termination hooks are best effort by default, a timed-out or abandoned hook leads to immediate termination, and an instance lifecycle policy can be combined for retention.
The quote states a termination hook extends the life of an instance already selected for termination, to complete in-progress work or save progress and transfer it to another instance.
The quote states zonal balance takes precedence, the policy is applied to the imbalanced zone first, and across all zones when balanced.
Under the mixed instances heading the quote states it first identifies which purchase option to terminate from the group settings so the group trends toward the specified Spot and On-Demand ratio.
The quote defines AllocationStrategy as aligning the remaining instances to the allocation strategy of the terminating purchase type, useful when preferred instance types have changed.
The quote defines ClosestToNextInstanceHour as terminating instances closest to the next billing hour to maximize use of hourly-charged instances.
The quote defines NewestInstance as terminating the newest instance, useful when testing a new launch configuration you don't want to keep in production.
The quote defines OldestInstance as terminating the oldest instance, useful when upgrading the group's instances to a new EC2 instance type.
The quote states noncurrent launch template instances are terminated first, followed by instances on the oldest version of the current launch template.
The quote states termination policies apply only to instances not considered unhealthy, and unhealthy instances bypass termination policy evaluation.
The quotes name two ways: SNS (launch or terminate notifications, only on or off) and EventBridge (notifications matched to criteria and sent to a variety of targets).
The quote states unhealthy instances are terminated despite custom termination policies or scale-in protection, and the only prevention is suspending HealthCheck, ReplaceUnhealthy or Terminate.

The quote supports up to 10 percent at a time, but the note right below says small groups are replaced one at a time (which can exceed 10 percent) and that 10 percent is a default changeable with an instance maintenance policy; the claim states 'at most' without either condition.
The quote states unhealthy instances are replaced after the instances finish warming up and the group has risen to more than 90 percent of desired capacity.
The quote states that when 10 percent is less than one, unhealthy instances are replaced one at a time, which might result in some downtime.
The quote states that with a scaling activity in progress and the group short of desired capacity by 10 percent or more, it waits for that activity before replacing unhealthy instances.
The quote states the group maintains a fixed number of instances, terminating an unhealthy instance and launching another to replace it.
The quotes support resizing an instance by changing its instance type and paying the new type's rate, but they never use or define the term 'vertical scaling', which the claim states as a definition.
The quote supports that you must stop an EBS-backed instance to change its type and should plan for downtime, but it does not mention 'vertical scaling', which the claim names.
The quote states a stopped instance in an Auto Scaling group is marked unhealthy and might be replaced, and that you can suspend the group's scaling processes to prevent this.
The Well-Architected quotes state attribute-based selection lets you automatically use newer generation instance types and access a broader range of Spot capacity.

The quote states automatic recovery replaces failed hardware and restarts the instance when the application cannot be deployed in multiple locations; context gives the reboot-tolerance condition the qualifier carries.

The quotes state Auto Scaling can self-heal stateless applications and add or remove capacity, and that stateless services prevent loss of data or availability on restart, where the context says the entire resource is replaced.
